Rashi on Gittin 69b:10:1.english: For the spleen - [Referring to one] whose spleen is swollen and enlarged due to illness:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:10:2.hebrew: שב ביני דמיא - שבע עלוקות של מים, בלעז שנשוא"ש:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:10:2.english: Seven water worms - Seven water leeches; in Old French: sansues:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:10:3.english: A female goat that has not opened [its womb] - A goat that has not given birth:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:10:4.english: And let him stand opposite it - he should stand across from it:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:10:5.english: And if not - [i.e.,] if there is no oven:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:11:1.english: Let him plaster it - [referring to] that spleen:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:11:2.hebrew: ביבי אורבי - יטיח אותו בכותל, וידבק בין שורות הכותל, וייבש שם:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:11:2.english: Between the bricks - He should plaster it onto the wall, and it will adhere between the rows [of bricks] of the wall, and dry there:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:11:3.english: And let him say this - "Just as this spleen dries, etc.":

Rashi on Gittin 69b:11:4.english: Let him search for a corpse - He should take the trouble until he knows where there is a dead person who died on Shabbat:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:11:5.english: Let him search - [This is] an expression of searching [and investigation].

Rashi on Gittin 69b:11:6.english: And let him take his hand - of the deceased:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:11:7.english: And let him place [it] opposite the spleen - of the sick person:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:12:2.english: And let him roast it in the fire of the blacksmith's house - let him roast it on the coals in front of the blacksmith:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:12:3.english: Water from the blacksmith's house - that [water] in which he quenches the iron:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:13:1.hebrew: ליפתח חביתא דחמרא לשמיה - יקנה חבית של יין לשתייתו, כלומר ישתה יין טוב תמיד הרבה:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:13:1.english: Let him open a barrel of wine for his sake - [He should] buy a barrel of wine for his [own] drinking, that is to say, he should regularly drink plenty of good wine:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:13:2.hebrew: לא אתי קמי דמר - לשאל רפואה, שהיין רפואה לו:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:13:2.english: He will not come before [my] Master - to ask for a remedy, for wine is a remedy for him:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:14:10.hebrew: ובדעמר גופנא - שהן חמים בסתוא, וישים באותו מקום:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:14:10.english: And [in rags] of cotton - for they are warm, in the winter, and he should place [them] in that place:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:14:2.english: Akukya - An herb whose name is kakoli:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:14:5.hebrew: מרתכא - קוגילו"ן, והוא מפסולת הכסף, שחופרין כסף מן הקרקע ויוצקים אותו, ומעלה ריתחא, והוא מרתחא:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:14:5.english: Silver dross [martekha] - kogilon [in Old French], and it is from the dross of silver, when they dig silver from the ground and smelt it, and it brings up froth [ritḥa], and that is marteḥa [martekha]:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:14:6.hebrew: חומרתא דפילון - בוטון שהנשים תולות בצואריהן, של זהב או של כסף, ונותן בו שמן שמעורב בו מין בושם ששמו פילון, ודומה לעלי גפנים, כדתניא בת"כ: "שלא יערב קימוס במר, מי גלובקיא בשמן, עלי גפנים בפילון":
Rashi on Gittin 69b:14:6.english: Chumreta defilon - A button [boton, i.e., a small pendant] of gold or of silver that women hang around their necks, and one puts into it oil in which is mixed a type of spice called pilon, and it resembles vine leaves, as it is taught in Torat Kohanim: "One shall not mix kimos in myrrh, mei glovkia in oil, [or] vine leaves in pilon":

Rashi on Gittin 69b:14:7.hebrew: ושייפא דחמימתא - צואת יונים, ולשון מורי: צואת תרנגולין:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:14:7.english: And sheyafa deḥamimta - pigeon droppings; and [in] my teacher's wording: chicken droppings:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:14:8.english: And let him take - all of these [ingredients]:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:14:9.english: In linen rags - for they are cool [and therefore used] in the summer:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:15:1.english: For shigrona - [This is] an illness of the thighs and the hips, which is called hanche [in Old French]:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:15:2.english: Patya demuninei - a vessel full of brine of small fish:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:15:3.hebrew: ולגנדריה שתין זמני אהא מטחתא - יגלגלו ששים פעמים על ירך זה, למעלה בקילבוסת שקורין הנק"א:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:15:3.english: And roll it sixty times on this thigh - He should roll it sixty times on this thigh, higher up on the haunch, which is called hanche [hip, in Old French]:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:16:1.english: For tzemirta - a stone that grows in the urinary tract and blocks the urine:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:16:3.hebrew: משחא דכופרא - פסולת של זפת, והוא עיטרן:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:16:3.english: Tar oil [mishcha dekufra] - [It is] the residue of pitch, and it is tar:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:16:4.english: Itzra dekaratei - The squeezing of leeks:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:17:1.english: Ona dezika - The ear [i.e., handle] of a wineskin:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:17:2.hebrew: חוטא דזהוריתא דשדתי' דומה בת דומה - חוט של זהורית שטואתו אשה חשודה, בת חשודה:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:17:2.english: A crimson thread spun by a dumah, daughter of a dumah - A thread of crimson that a woman suspected [of promiscuity], daughter of a suspected [woman], spun:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:18:1.english: On a dry sisna [asisna yevishta] - on a dry thornbush:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:18:2.english: And let him examine the stone that comes out of him - He should be careful with the stone that emerges from him, to preserve it:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:18:3.english: As it is effective for all fevers - [This refers to] an illness that they call *fevre* [fever]:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:19:3.english: Atraf adara - Leaves of a tree whose name is adar:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:19:5.hebrew: וכי שתי - דקיימא לן: הרוחץ בחמין שותה מהם, והם רפואה לו, במסכת שבת (דף מא.):
Rashi on Gittin 69b:19:5.english: And when he drinks - For it is established for us [that] one who bathes in hot water drinks [some] of it, and it is a remedy for him, [as stated] in Tractate Shabbat (41a):

Rashi on Gittin 69b:19:6.hebrew: ממיא דאדרא - לישתי, אבל ממיא דסופלי לא לישתי:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:19:6.english: From the water of the eder [tree] - he should drink, but from the water of the date pits he should not drink:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:19:7.english: That they cause infertility - they make him sterile, [unable] to beget [children]:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:1:1.english: And let him drip it on three stalks of cabbage - He should drip it onto three stalks of cabbage in a vessel:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:1:2.english: And let him stir it with a sprig of marmehin - [He should] stir the pot with a twig of a tree whose name is marmehin:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:1:3.english: Feces of a white dog - Excrement of a white dog:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:1:4.english: And let him mix [it] with balm - [This means] balsam:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:1:5.english: And as much as possible - for him [to manage] with another remedy or to endure his illness:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:1:6.english: Let him not eat the feces - He should not eat the feces of the dogs:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:1:7.english: Because it separates - [it] detaches his limbs:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:20:2.english: From seven furrows - From seven garden beds:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:20:3.english: With their dirt - [the] dirt that comes up with their roots:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:2:1.english: For gira - an illness called espointe [in Old French, a sharp, stinging pain]:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:2:2.hebrew: גירא דליליתא - חץ של לילית, אבן שעשויה כחץ ונופלת עם הברד:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:2:2.english: Gira deLilita - An arrow of Lilith, a stone that is shaped like an arrow and falls with the hail:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:2:3.english: And let him turn it upside down - [With] the point downward and the handle upward:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:2:4.english: And let him be careful about [leaving the water] uncovered - that it be in a place where a snake is not found:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:2:5.hebrew: אנפקא - זהו רביעית, וכן שם הכלי:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:2:5.english: Anpaka - This is a revi'it [a quarter-log], and [it is] also the name of the vessel:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:3:1.english: For a pus-filled wound - [In Old French,] clou [a boil or abscess]:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:3:2.hebrew: אהלא תלאנא - אהלות אדום, כמין תולעת שני:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:3:2.english: Ahala tolana - Red aloes, like crimson [lit., the scarlet worm]:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:4:1.hebrew: לפירחא דליבא - שלבו פורח, פשמיי"ר בלע"ז:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:4:1.english: For fluttering of the heart - [meaning] that his heart flutters, pasmer [to faint] in Old French:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:4:3.hebrew: ונשטרינהו בכמכא - ישרה אותם בכותח, טרכנריי"ד בלע"ז:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:4:3.english: And let him soak them in kamka - He should soak them in kutach [a fermented dairy and bread dip], terchanreid in Old French:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:4:4.english: From which forty days have not passed - [since] the kutach was made:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:4:6.english: His heart will palpitate - For all of these [foods] are weak things, and they sap a person's strength:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:4:7.english: For heaviness of the heart - [meaning] that his heart is heavy upon him:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:7:1.english: Of these of ours - our peppers.

Rashi on Gittin 69b:8:2.hebrew: אטרפה דעראה - עלה של עץ ארע שקורין לוריי"ר, ופריו קורין ביי"ש:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:8:2.english: Atarpa de'ara'ah - A leaf of the ar'a [laurel] tree, which is called laurier [in Old French], and its fruit is called baies [berries]:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:8:4.english: And let him tie it in a shistag - He should tie it in a piece of cotton cloth:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:8:5.english: And let him be careful of the seed - He should be careful not to swallow the grain of the seed:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:9:3.english: To loosen - to loosen [the bowels of] a constipated person:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:9:4.english: And your mnemonic - so that you do not confuse [them], drinking wet [chamomile] to loosen [the bowels] and dry [chamomile] to bind [them]:

Rashi on Gittin 69b:9:5.hebrew: איצא - שם עשב, וכשהוא לח סוכרין בו נהרות, כך הלח סותם:
Rashi on Gittin 69b:9:5.english: Itza - [This is] the name of a grass, and when it is wet, people dam rivers with it; so [too], the wet [one] stops up [the bowels]:
